title: What Does the Room Reward?
headline: How the People Around You Shape What You Want
tagline: Whatever a community consistently celebrates, it quietly teaches people to pursue.
seo_title: How the People Around You Shape What You Want (John 12:43) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Every room has a reward system: approval, laughter, status. A devotional for men on John 12:42-43 and Galatians 1:10 about the desires a group teaches.
verse_text: Many even among the leaders believed in him. But because of the Pharisees they would not openly acknowledge their faith…. for they loved human praise more than praise from God.

scriptures.text: Many even among the leaders believed in him. But because of the Pharisees they would not openly acknowledge their faith…. for they loved human praise more than praise from God.
Am I now trying to win the approval of human beings, or of God?

items: Every room has a reward system.

blocks.text: A man walks into a group and quickly begins learning:

items: The room doesn’t need a written policy.
But who taught you to value it?
Some leaders believed in Jesus but would not acknowledge Him publicly.
“They loved human praise more than praise from God.”
Sometimes you don’t realize how badly you want the reward until obedience threatens to take it away.
If every mention of money impresses the room, money begins feeling like significance.
If stories of conquest get laughter, lust gets social reinforcement.
If everyone admires nonstop work, exhaustion starts looking like importance.
If vulnerability gets awkward silence but accomplishment gets celebration, men learn:
show your success, hide your struggle.

blocks.text: Whatever a community consistently celebrates, it quietly teaches people to pursue.

items: make me a brother who rewards what You value.
Let my presence help make Christlikeness honorable in the room.
You discover which audience matters most when the audiences disagree.
What has this room taught me to want?
